faqItems.q: Are there really no hidden fees?
faqItems.a: Nothing is added unless you choose it. The daily rate covers the vehicle for up to 5 people plus third-party liability insurance. At pickup we offer two optional extras and you are free to decline both: a fuel service fee, if you would rather not refuel the vehicle yourself, and collision coverage for the rental vehicle itself, which covers 90% of its value — the included liability insurance covers damage to third parties only.

faqItems.q: What if I have never driven a manual?
faqItems.a: Our buggies are automatic, so there is nothing to learn. Cozumel traffic is not the place to practise a clutch.

faqItems.q: Can I drive the whole island?
faqItems.a: Almost. The coastal road covers roughly two thirds of Cozumel — the part with the beaches, the cenotes and the lookouts. The remaining third is a protected nature reserve, open to authorised personnel only.
Message Dani on WhatsApp. That is not a marketing line: it is the same number that answers while you are on the road.

terms.title: Terms & Conditions
terms.intro: These terms govern every rental with Buggy Rentals with Dani in Cozumel, Quintana Roo, Mexico. By booking, you agree to them.
terms.questionsDesc: Message us on WhatsApp and we'll explain anything that isn't clear — before you book.

sections.heading: 1. Driver requirements
sections.body: The driver must be at least 18 years old and hold a valid driver's license (any country). We record the license number at booking and verify the physical license at pickup. Driving under the influence of alcohol or drugs voids all coverage and terminates the rental immediately.

sections.heading: 2. Booking and deposit
sections.body: A $25 USD deposit per vehicle secures your reservation. The remaining balance is due at pickup, in cash (USD or MXN) or by card. The deposit is applied to your total — it is not an extra charge.

sections.heading: 3. Cancellations and no-shows
sections.body: Cancel at least 48 hours before your rental date and the deposit is fully refunded. Cancellations inside 48 hours, and no-shows, forfeit the deposit. If your cruise ship fails to dock in Cozumel for any reason, your deposit is refunded in full — just send us the proof.

sections.heading: 4. What the price includes
sections.body: The daily rate covers the vehicle for up to 5 people, third-party liability insurance, and a full tank of fuel at pickup. It does not cover fuel consumed during your rental, traffic fines, parking fees, or damage to the rented vehicle itself.

sections.heading: 5. Insurance and liability
sections.body: Liability insurance covers damage you cause to third parties. It does not cover damage to the rented vehicle, theft, or personal injury. You are financially responsible for damage to the vehicle while it is in your care. We strongly recommend checking whether your travel insurance or credit card covers rental vehicles abroad.

sections.heading: 6. Fuel policy
sections.body: Vehicles are delivered with a full tank and must be returned full. If the vehicle is returned with less fuel, the difference is charged at the local pump price plus a $10 USD service fee.

sections.heading: 7. Use of the vehicle
sections.body: The vehicle may be driven only on paved and marked roads on Cozumel island, only by the registered driver, and only within the agreed rental period. Off-roading, beach driving, towing, racing, and transporting more than 5 occupants are prohibited and void all coverage.

sections.heading: 8. Traffic violations
sections.body: You are responsible for any traffic fine, ticket, or penalty issued during your rental period, including those that arrive after the vehicle is returned.

sections.heading: 9. Returns and late fees
sections.body: Vehicles must be returned by 5:00 PM on the agreed return date. Late returns are charged at one quarter of the daily rate per hour, up to a full extra day.

sections.heading: 10. Hotel delivery
sections.body: Delivery is available free of charge to select resorts on the island, subject to availability and confirmed by us after booking. If we cannot deliver to your hotel we will tell you before your rental date and you may cancel for a full refund.

sections.heading: 11. Breakdowns and assistance
sections.body: If the vehicle fails through no fault of yours, contact us on WhatsApp immediately. We will repair or replace it as fast as we can, or refund the unused portion of your rental. We are not liable for indirect costs such as missed tours, taxis, or a missed cruise departure.

sections.heading: 12. Privacy
sections.body: We collect only the data needed to process your booking: name, email, phone, driver's license number, and your stay or cruise details. We do not sell or share it with third parties, except payment processing through Stripe. Write to us to request deletion of your data.

sections.heading: 13. Applicable law
sections.body: These terms are governed by the laws of Mexico, with jurisdiction in the courts of Cozumel, Quintana Roo.

drivingGuide.heroDesc: The unofficial survival manual for exploring paradise on four wheels. No textbooks required — just read this before you hit the road.
drivingGuide.heroAlt: A pink open-top rental buggy parked on the coastal road beside the turquoise Cozumel shoreline

m1.title: Crack the Grid
m1.subtitle: San Miguel's street system isn't random — it's a puzzle. Solve it once, navigate forever.
m1.avenidasBody: Start at the seafront with Av. Rafael E. Melgar, then count inland in multiples of 5: 5a Av, 10a Av, 15a Av…
m1.avenidasRule: Right of way — always yield to them
m1.callesBody: The spine is Av. Juárez. North of it = even numbers (2, 4, 6…). South = odd numbers (1, 3, 5…).
m1.callesRule: Full stop — no yield, no rolling through
m1.noteBody: Forget traffic lights. One-way direction is shown by tiny arrows painted on building corners or low poles. Check them before you turn — nearly every block alternates direction.
m1.photoAlt: A street in downtown San Miguel with shops at ground level and vehicles parked along the kerb
m1.photoCaption: Downtown San Miguel, where the grid starts.

m2.title: The Golden Rules
m2.subtitle: Driving here is chill — as long as you know the three things that will trip you up.

rules.title: The red disco — full stop
rules.body: "Alto" means your vehicle stops completely. Not a California roll, not a slow creep — a full stop. Local police specifically watch tourists at these. You've been warned.

rules.title: Roundabouts — traffic inside has priority
rules.body: If cars are already circling, you wait. Pull up, stop fully, and merge only when there's a clear gap. No honking, no forcing it.

rules.title: The moto swarm — eyes on mirrors
rules.body: Cozumel has more motorcycles per capita than almost anywhere in Mexico. They weave right, pass in blind spots, and materialize out of nowhere. Check your mirrors three times before changing lanes or opening your door.

m2.photoAlt: An open-top rental vehicle carrying passengers along a downtown Cozumel street

m3.title: The Anti-Ticket Playbook
m3.subtitle: Don't be the tourist who loses a morning at City Hall. Two rules cover 95% of situations.
m3.parkBody: Yellow or red kerbs = no parking, ever. In Cozumel they don't leave a ticket on your windshield — the police take your rear license plate. Getting it back means a trip to the Municipal Palace plus a hefty fine. Not worth it.
m3.pulledOverBody: Stay calm. If you broke a rule, the officer must issue a written ticket. Never offer cash on the street. Just say:
m3.pulledOverQuote: Por favor, oficial, levante la infracción.
m3.pulledOverAfter: Pay it at the municipal treasury within a few days and you get a 50% discount plus immediate plate return.
m3.noteBody: Never hand money to a police officer on the street. It's called a mordida and it only makes things worse. Ask for the written infraction — that's your right.

m4.title: Gas Station Survival
m4.subtitle: There are zero gas stations outside San Miguel. Fill up before you leave town — no exceptions.
m4.step1Body: Before the attendant puts the nozzle in — get out, look at the digital display, and confirm it reads $0.00. Don't skip this.
m4.step2Body: Our pickup and drop-off point is right at a gas station — so at the end of your day, we'll help you fill up and return the tank exactly as you got it. No stress, no guesswork.

m5.title: Hidden Hazards
m5.subtitle: Two things nobody warns you about. Both will ruin your day if you're not ready.
m5.topesBody: Mexican speed bumps aren't polite little humps. They're designed to absolutely stop you. Many on beach roads aren't painted. Hit one at speed in a buggy and you'll feel it in your spine. Slow down approaching beach club entrances and residential zones.
m5.cruiseTitle: Cruise ship traffic — watch your timing
m5.cruiseBody: Cozumel is the number one cruise destination in the Caribbean. The area near the piers gets busy — keep in mind that traffic picks up when passengers start heading back to their ships.

m7.title: The Wild East Coast
m7.subtitle: Cross the island on the Transversal highway and you enter another world. Read this first.
m7.signalBody: You'll lose 90% of cell service on the east coast. One straight road — hard to get lost. Download offline maps before you leave town.
m7.swimBody: Beautiful beaches with dangerous rip currents. Only swim at Chen Río or Punta Morena — natural rock pools, totally calm.
m7.wildlifeBody: You're in a nature reserve. Giant iguanas, coatis, and in rainy season (Jun–Sep) thousands of blue crabs migrating across the road. Slow down.
m7.noteBody: The east coast highway is one of the most scenic drives in the Caribbean. Pack water, a charged camera, and your offline map. Then just drive.
m7.photoAlt: Aerial view of a road cutting straight through the Cozumel jungle, with a buggy pulled over on the shoulder
m7.photoCaption: The east coast road — one lane, no signal, no crowds.
